Sara liked to write stories. She wrote with her crayons on paper. She wrote about animals, princesses, and adventures. She was very good at writing.

One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a big rail near the swings. The rail was for trains to go on. Sara wanted to write on the rail. She thought it would be fun.

She took out her crayon and started to write her name on the rail. She did not see the sign that said "Do not write on the rail". She did not hear her mom calling her.

"Stop, Sara, stop!" her mom said. "You cannot write on the rail. It is not yours. It is for the trains. The trains need the rail to be clean and safe. If you write on the rail, you can make the trains crash. That is very bad."

Sara felt sorry. She did not know she was doing something wrong. She did not want to make the trains crash. She loved the trains. They were big and fast and reliable. They always came on time.

"I'm sorry, mom," Sara said. "I did not mean to be bad. I just wanted to write. I like to write."

"I know, Sara, I know," her mom said. "Writing is good. But you have to write on the right things. You can write on paper, or on a board, or on a book. But you cannot write on things that are not yours, or that can hurt others. Do you understand?"

Sara nodded. She understood. She learned a lesson. She hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. Thank you for teaching me."

"I love you too, Sara," her mom said. "And I'm proud of you for learning. Now, let's go home and write a story together. How about a story about a train?"

Sara smiled. She liked that idea. She liked to write stories. And she liked to write on the right things.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big red truck. The truck has a hose and a ladder. It is a fire truck.

"Wow, look at the fire truck!" Tom says. "I want to own it. It is so cool."

"No, I want to own it. It is so pretty." Mia says. They both run to the fire truck.

A fireman is sitting in the truck. He smiles at Tom and Mia. He says, "Hello, kids. Do you like the fire truck?"

"Yes, we like it very much. Can we own it?" Tom and Mia ask.

The fireman laughs. He says, "Sorry, kids. You cannot own the fire truck. It belongs to the fire station. We use it to put out fires and help people."

Tom and Mia are sad. They really want to own the fire truck. The fireman says, "But you can touch it and look at it. Do you want to see the hose and the ladder?"

Tom and Mia nod. They are happy again. The fireman shows them the hose and the ladder. He says, "Be careful. The hose can spray water very fast. And the ladder can go very high."

Tom and Mia touch the hose and the ladder. They are amazed. They say, "Thank you, fireman. You are very nice."

The fireman says, "You are welcome, kids. But now I have to go. There is a fire somewhere. I have to help."

He turns on the siren and the lights. The fire truck makes a loud noise. Tom and Mia cover their ears. They wave goodbye to the fireman. They say, "Bye, fire truck. Bye, fireman. Be safe."

The fire truck drives away. Tom and Mia go back to the park. They see a big ice cream truck. The ice cream truck has many flavors and colors. It is a sweet truck.

"Wow, look at the ice cream truck!" Tom says. "I want to own it. It is so yummy."

"No, I want to own it. It is so tasty." Mia says. They both run to the ice cream truck.

The ice cream man is sitting in the truck. He smiles at Tom and Mia. He says, "Hello, kids. Do you like the ice cream truck?"

"Yes, we like it very much. Can we own it?" Tom and Mia ask.

The ice cream man laughs. He says, "Sorry, kids. You cannot own the ice cream truck. It belongs to me. I use it to sell ice cream and make money."

Tom and Mia are sad. They really want to own the ice cream truck. The ice cream man says, "But you can buy some ice cream and eat it. Do you want to try some flavors and colors?"

Tom and Mia nod. They are happy again. The ice cream man gives them each a cone with two scoops of ice cream. Tom chooses chocolate and vanilla. Mia chooses strawberry and mint. They are delicious.

Tom and Mia lick their ice cream. They are satisfied. They say, "Thank you, ice cream man. You are very nice."

The ice cream man says, "You are welcome, kids. But be careful. The ice cream can melt and drip. And it can be very cold and hot."

Tom and Mia are confused. They say, "Cold and hot? How can ice cream be cold and hot?"

The ice cream man says, "Well, ice cream is cold because it is frozen. But it can also be hot because it has sugar. Sugar can make your mouth hot and hurt your teeth. So you have to eat ice cream slowly and brush your teeth later."

Tom and Mia understand. They say, "Oh, we see. We will eat ice cream slowly and brush our teeth later."

They eat their ice cream slowly and enjoy it. They do not want to make their mouth hot and hurt their teeth. They are smart kids. They finish their ice cream and throw away their cones. They say, "Bye, ice cream truck. Bye, ice cream man. Have a good day."

The ice cream truck drives away. Tom and Mia go back to the park. They play some more. They have fun. They are happy. They are friends. The end.

Tom did not listen to his mom. He ran out of the house with his bat and ball. He did not say sorry or thank you. He was ignorant of his mom's words and love. He went to the park to play cricket with his friends.

"Please, duck, come and eat. We have more bread for you," Tom said.

But the duck did not listen. It looked at them and quacked.

Sara and Tom felt sad. They wanted to make friends with the duck. They decided to try one more time. They threw the last piece of bread right in front of the duck. They hoped it would come.

The duck looked at the bread. It looked at Sara and Tom. It saw that they were kind and patient. It decided to trust them. It swam slowly to the bread and ate it.

Sara and Tom were very happy. They cheered and waved.

"Thank you, duck, for eating our bread. You are a nice duck. We like you," Sara said.

The duck quacked and nodded. It liked Sara and Tom too. It stayed with them for a while. They fed it more bread and stroked its feathers.

Mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of Sara and Tom. They had learned how to be patient and friendly with the duck. They had made a new friend.

He pointed his staff at a table and said the spell. The table vanished. Tom was happier. He pointed his staff at a window and said the spell. The window vanished. Tom was happiest.

But then, Tom heard his teacher coming back. He was scared. He did not want his teacher to see what he had done. He quickly hid the book and the staff behind his back. His teacher came in and saw the empty room. He was angry. He asked Tom what he had done. Tom lied and said he did not know. His teacher did not believe him. He used his own staff to find the book and the staff behind Tom's back. He took them from Tom and scolded him. He told him that he was foolish and naughty. He told him that the spell he used was dangerous and hard to undo. He told him that he had to work hard to bring back the things he had vanished. He told him that he had to learn to be patient and respectful.

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He wished he had listened to his teacher. He wished he had not been impatient. He wished he had not used the spell. He learned his lesson. He said sorry to his teacher and asked for his help. His teacher forgave him and helped him. They worked together to bring back the chair, the table and the window. It took a long time and a lot of effort, but they did it. Tom was relieved and grateful. He promised his teacher that he would never do such a thing again. He promised his teacher that he would follow his advice and practice the small and easy magic first. He became a better and happier wizard.

"There, now he can talk!" Tom says. "Can you hear us, Mr. Snowman?"

The snowman still does not say anything. He is icy and cold. He cannot talk.

Lily and Tom are sad. They want the snowman to be their friend. They hug him and try to warm him up.

"Please, Mr. Snowman, say something!" Lily says. "We want to play with you. We want to hear your voice."

The snowman feels their love. He feels a little bit warm. He tries to talk.

"Hello, Lily. Hello, Tom." The snowman says in a low voice. "Thank you for making me. Thank you for your love. You are very kind."

Lily and Tom are happy. They hear the snowman's voice. They smile and clap their hands.

"Yay, Mr. Snowman, you can talk!" Tom says. "We are your friends. We will play with you every day."

The snowman is happy too. He has friends. He has a voice. He is not icy and cold anymore. He is warm and alive.

They heard a voice behind them. It was Mom. She saw the broken block and the sad faces. She frowned and shook her head.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They did not want to tell Mom. They were afraid she would be angry. They pointed at their noses. They lied.

Mom looked at their noses. They were not red or hurt. She knew they were lying. She did not like lies. She crossed her arms and tapped her foot.

"Really? Your noses snapped?" Mom asked.

Tom and Lily nodded. They hoped Mom would believe them. But Mom did not. She smiled and winked.

"Then, I guess I have to snap your noses back," Mom said.

She reached for their noses and pinched them gently. Tom and Lily squealed and giggled. They felt Mom's tickles. They forgot about the broken block. They hugged Mom and said sorry.

"It's okay, my loves. But next time, don't lie and don't fight. Share your blocks and play nicely," Mom said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They said yes, Mom. They kissed Mom and thanked her. They picked up the blocks and played again. They shared the blocks and played nicely. They were happy and Mom was happy. The end.

They tug and pull on the bone. The bone is tight in their mouths. They cannot let go.

A boy sees them. He is kind. He wants to help them.

"Hey, dogs, stop fighting!" he says. "I have a treat for you."

He shows them a bag of cookies. The cookies smell good. Lily and Max look at the cookies. They want the cookies.

They drop the bone. They run to the boy. The boy gives them each a cookie. They wag their tails. They are happy.

The boy picks up the bone. He throws it far away. Lily and Max chase the bone. They play with the bone. They share the bone.

They thank the boy. The boy smiles. He is happy too.

Tom likes to read books. He has many books in his room. He reads about cars, animals, and space. He reads every day before he sleeps.

One day, Tom finds a new book in his room. It is a big book with a picture of a fish on the cover. Tom likes fish. He opens the book and sees many words and pictures. He wants to read the book.

He asks his mom, "Mom, can you read this book to me?"

Mom smiles and says, "Sure, Tom. This is a book about fishing. Do you know what fishing is?"

Tom shakes his head. He does not know what fishing is.

Mom says, "Fishing is when you catch fish from the water. You need a rod, a line, and a hook. You put a worm on the hook and throw the line in the water. Then you wait for a fish to bite the hook. When you feel a tug, you pull the rod and catch the fish."

Tom listens and looks at the pictures. He sees a man with a rod and a fish. He thinks fishing looks fun.

He says, "Mom, can we go fishing?"

Mom says, "Maybe someday, Tom. But fishing is not easy. You need to be patient and quiet. And sometimes it is cold and wet. You need to wear warm clothes and boots."

Tom nods. He understands. He says, "Thank you, Mom, for reading to me. I like this book. I want to learn more about fishing."

Mom hugs him and says, "You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad you like this book. Maybe we can go to the library and find more books about fishing. Would you like that?"

Tom smiles and says, "Yes, Mom. I would like that very much."

Lily ran to the boy and told him to stop. She said, "Stop teasing the giraffe. It is not nice. The giraffe is not a toy. It is a living animal. It has feelings. You are hurting it. You should be kind to animals. They are our friends."

The boy was surprised. He did not expect Lily to stand up to him. He felt ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry. I was just having fun. I did not mean to hurt the giraffe. You are right. I should be kind to animals. They are our friends."

Lily smiled. She said, "It's okay. You can say sorry to the giraffe. Maybe it will forgive you. Maybe it will let you pet it and feed it some leaves. Maybe you can be friends with the giraffe."

The boy nodded. He said, "Okay. Let's go and say sorry to the giraffe. Maybe we can be friends with the giraffe. And maybe we can be friends with each other too."

Nemo swam around, looking for some food to eat. Suddenly, he saw a big shadow coming towards him. It was the bad shark! Nemo was so scared and didn't know what to do. But then he remembered what his mommy told him. He had to protect himself.

Nemo swam as fast as he could, trying to get away from the bad shark. But he was running out of oxygen and couldn't swim anymore. Just when he thought he was going to be eaten by the bad shark, he saw a big rock. Nemo swam towards the rock and hid behind it. The bad shark couldn't find him and swam away.

From that day on, Nemo always remembered to protect himself and stay safe from the bad shark. He also made sure to always have enough oxygen so he could swim away if he needed to.

Tom and Lily were safe in the hole. They met other rabbits who welcomed them and shared their food. They found a cozy nest and cuddled together. They thanked each other for being brave and smart. Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. One day, they saw a big package on the table. It had a label that said "To Mom and Dad, from Grandma and Grandpa". They wondered what was inside.

"Let's open it and see!" Ben said. He climbed on a chair and reached for the package.

"No, Ben, we can't!" Lily said. "It's not for us. It's for Mom and Dad. And look, it says 'delicate'. That means it can break easily. We have to be careful."

But Ben did not listen. He pulled the package and it fell on the floor. It made a loud noise and something inside cracked.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben said. They heard Mom and Dad coming. They were scared.

Mom and Dad saw the package on the floor. They opened it and saw a beautiful vase that Grandma and Grandpa had sent them. But it was broken into many pieces.

"What happened?" Mom asked. "Who did this?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry. They knew they had done something bad.

"It was me," Ben said. "I wanted to see what was inside. I'm sorry, Mom and Dad. I didn't mean to break it."

Mom and Dad were sad and angry. But they also saw that Ben was honest and brave. They hugged him and Lily.

The moral of the story is: You should not touch things that are not yours and you should be careful with delicate things. You should also listen to your siblings and tell the truth when you make a mistake.

Lily took Tom to their mom. Their mom saw Tom's finger and said, "Oh, no, what happened?" Lily explained what happened. She said, "We found a snake in the garden. Tom wanted to touch it. I told him not to. But he did not listen. The snake bit him."

Their mom said, "Oh, Tom, you should have listened to Lily. She was right. Snakes can be harmful. You are lucky it was not a poisonous snake. You could have been very sick. Come on, let's go to the doctor. He will make your finger better."

Tom said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. I learned my lesson. I will not touch snakes again."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your friends and family when they warn you about something. They care about you and want you to be safe. Do not play with things that can hurt you. Respect the animals and their space.

One day, a big lion was very hungry. He walked around the forest, looking for food. He saw a small rabbit, hiding under a bush. The lion thought, "This rabbit will be a tasty snack for me." He opened his mouth and roared very loud.

The rabbit was very scared. He said, "Please, Mr. Lion, do not eat me. I am too small and bony. You will not be full. Why don't you look for a bigger animal, like a deer or a zebra?"

The lion was very rude. He said, "I do not care. I want to eat you now. You are easy to catch and I am very hungry. Stop talking and get in my mouth."

The rabbit had an idea. He said, "Wait, Mr. Lion, I have something to show you. It is very beautiful and shiny. You will like it more than me. Follow me and I will show you."

The lion was curious. He said, "What is it? Where is it?" He followed the rabbit, hoping to see something nice.

The rabbit led the lion to a big lake. He said, "Look, Mr. Lion, there it is. The most beautiful and shiny thing in the forest. It is your own reflection in the water. See how big and strong you are. You are the king of the forest. You do not need to eat me. You can eat anything you want."

The lion looked at the water and saw himself. He was very proud. He said, "You are right, little rabbit. I am the most beautiful and shiny thing in the forest. I am the king of the forest. I do not need to eat you. You are too small and bony. You can go and live your life. Thank you for showing me this."

The rabbit was very happy. He said, "You are welcome, Mr. Lion. I am glad you are not rude anymore. You are very wise and kind. I hope you find a good meal soon. Goodbye, Mr. Lion."

The lion and the rabbit parted ways. The lion learned a lesson. He learned that being rude and greedy is not good. He learned that being curious and humble is better. He learned that sometimes, a small and bony rabbit can have a big and clever idea.

Mom looked at the thermometer. She said, "Oh, Lily, you have a fever. You need to drink some water and take some medicine. And you need to rest. No TV for now. You can read a book or listen to some music."

Lily did not like what Mom said. She wanted to watch TV. She was bored and restless. She said, "But Mom, I don't want to rest. I want to watch TV. TV makes me happy. Please, Mom, can I watch TV?"

Mom shook her head. She said, "No, Lily, you can't watch TV. TV is not good for you when you are sick. It will make your eyes tired and your head hurt more. You need to rest. Rest will make you better. I will come back soon and see how you are. Be a good girl and rest."

Mom kissed Lily and left the room. Lily sighed. She did not want to rest. She wanted to watch TV. But she knew Mom was right. Mom loved her and wanted her to be well. She picked up a book and tried to read. She hoped she would feel better soon.

They heard the bear sniffing and growling outside. It tried to paw at the tent, but it was too thick and strong. The bear gave up and walked away.

Lily and Ben felt relieved. They hugged Mom and Dad and thanked them.

"Can we go home now?" Ben asked.

"Sure, we can pack up and leave. But first, let's have some breakfast. You must be hungry." Dad said.

They ate some bread and jam and drank some milk. They packed up their tent and their things. They said goodbye to the big park and the bear. They drove home in their car. Lily and Ben were happy. They had a big adventure, but they also had a big hug.

One day, Sara finds something shiny in the sand. She picks it up and shows it to Ben. It is a silver ring. It has a pretty stone on it.

"Wow, Sara, you found a treasure!" Ben says. "Where did it come from?"

"I don't know, maybe someone lost it," Sara says. "It is very pretty. Do you want to try it on?"

Ben nods and puts the ring on his finger. It is too big for him. It falls off and rolls away.

"Oh no, where did it go?" Sara says. They look for the ring in the grass. They can't find it.

"Maybe a bird took it," Ben says. "Or a mouse. Or a worm."

Sara feels sad. She liked the ring. She wanted to keep it.

"Maybe we can find another one," Ben says. He sees Sara's face. He wants to make her happy. He has an idea.

He takes the shovel and the bucket. He digs a big hole in the sand. He puts some of his toys in the hole. He covers them with sand.

"Look, Sara, I made a treasure for you," he says. "You can dig it up and see what is inside."

Sara smiles. She takes the shovel and digs in the sand. She finds a car, a doll, a ball and a book. She is happy.

"Thank you, Ben, you are very kind," she says. "You are the best friend ever."

They hug and play with the toys. They forget about the silver ring. They have fun in the garden.

Tim and Lily were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they went to the park with their moms. There were many things to do at the park. They saw swings, slides, sand, and a big tree.

Tim and Lily ran to the tree. They saw a shiny thing on the ground. It was a ring. It had a red stone and a gold band. It was very pretty.

"Wow, look at this thing!" Tim said. He picked up the ring and put it on his finger. "It is mine now."

"No, it is not yours!" Lily said. "You did not bring it. You steal it. That is bad. Someone else lost it. They are sad. They want it back."

"I don't care. I like it. It is mine." Tim said. He ran away from Lily. He did not want to share.

Lily was angry and sad. She followed Tim. She wanted to make him give back the ring. She saw a lady sitting on a bench. The lady was crying. She had no ring on her finger.

"Excuse me, miss," Lily said. "Did you lose a thing? A ring with a red stone and a gold band?"

The lady looked at Lily. She nodded. "Yes, I did. It was my grandma's ring. She gave it to me before she died. It is very special to me. I was playing with it and it fell off. I can't find it. I am so poor without it."

Lily felt sorry for the lady. She pointed to Tim. "He has it. He steal it. He is bad. I will get it for you."

Lily ran to Tim. She grabbed his hand. She pulled the ring off his finger. She gave it to the lady.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" the lady said. She hugged Lily. She put the ring on her finger. She smiled. "You are very good. You are very kind. You are my hero."

Lily smiled too. She felt happy. She did the right thing. She looked at Tim. He was not happy. He was mad. He was sorry.

"I am sorry, miss," Tim said. "I am sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not steal. I should share. Can you forgive me?"

The lady and Lily nodded. They forgave Tim. They were all friends. They played together at the park. They had fun. They learned a lesson.

One evening, Anna's mom says, "It is time to go home, Ben. Say goodbye to Anna." Ben is sad. He does not want to go home. He wants to play more. He says, "No, I want to stay."

Anna's mom says, "You can come again tomorrow, Ben. But now you have to go. It is late and dark. You need to sleep." Ben is still sad. He does not like the dark. He is scared of the dark.

Anna sees that Ben is sad. She remembers that she has a flashlight. She runs to her room and gets it. She comes back and gives it to Ben. She says, "Here, Ben. You can have this. It is a flashlight. It makes light. You can use it when it is dark. Do not be scared."

Ben is surprised. He looks at the flashlight. He likes it. It is bright and shiny. He says, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend. I like the flashlight. It is cool." He hugs Anna.

Ben is happy. He looks at the car. He likes it. It is smooth and strong. He says, "Thank you, Anna. You are very nice. I like the car. It is fun." He puts the car and the flashlight in his bag. He says, "Goodbye, Anna. See you tomorrow."

Anna says, "Goodbye, Ben. See you tomorrow." She waves to him. He waves back. He goes with his mom. He is not sad anymore. He is not scared anymore. He has a flashlight and a car. He has a friend.

Anna goes with her mom. She is not sad anymore. She is not mad anymore. She has a doll and a flashlight. She has a friend.

They both smile. They both accept. They both share. They are both happy.

One day, a big dog comes to the yard. It has sharp teeth and loud bark. It runs to Lila and Tom. It wants to bite them. Lila and Tom are scared.

"Let's go, Lily!" Tom said. He ran to the hill and lay down on the leaves. He started to roll down.

"Wait for me, Tom!" Lily said. She ran after him and lay down on the leaves too. She started to roll down.

But then they saw a problem. There was a big rock at the bottom of the hill. They did not want to hit the rock. It would hurt.

"Stop, stop!" Tom yelled. He tried to stop rolling, but he could not. The leaves were too slippery. He was going too fast.

"Help, help!" Lily yelled. She tried to stop rolling too, but she could not. She was going too fast too.

They were getting closer and closer to the rock. They were scared.

But then they saw a friend. It was Ben, the dog. He was playing with a red sock. He saw Tom and Lily rolling down the hill. He saw the rock too. He wanted to help.

He ran to the rock and put the red sock on it. He hoped it would make the rock softer. He hoped it would make Tom and Lily stop.

Tom and Lily saw the red sock on the rock. They did not know why it was there, but they were glad. They hit the red sock and bounced off. They did not hit the rock. They did not get hurt.

They stopped rolling and got up. They were happy. They hugged Ben, the dog.

"Thank you, Ben!" Tom said. "You saved us!"

"Thank you, Ben!" Lily said. "You are a good friend!"

Ben, the dog, wagged his tail. He was happy too. He liked to play with Tom and Lily. He liked to share his red sock. He did not mind if it was dirty. He did not mind if it had holes. He liked to yield his red sock. He liked to be nice.

The cow, the pig, and the duck all worked together to help Mimi. They found more hay and fixed her fragile house. Mimi was so happy to see her friends help her. She said, "Thank you, friends! My house is good now."

From that day on, Mimi's house didn't vanish anymore. She was very happy to live in her hay house with her friends on the farm. They all played and had fun together every day. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, a brown dog named Max was playing in the park. He loved to run and jump. Max saw a big jar of jelly on a table. It was red and looked yummy. Max wanted to eat the jelly.

Max tried to get the jelly, but a big man said, "No, Max! That is not for you." Max was sad. He really wanted the jelly. He thought of a plan to get it.

Max saw a ball and had an idea. He took the ball and ran very fast. He rushed back to the table with the ball in his mouth. The big man saw Max and laughed. He said, "Good dog, Max!"

While the big man was looking at the ball, Max jumped on the table. He got the jelly and ate it all up. The big man was not happy, but Max was very happy. He got the jelly and it was yummy.

Tim and Lily were playing in the living room. They had many toys, but they liked the switch best. The switch was on the wall, and it made the light go on and off. Tim and Lily took turns to press the switch and laugh.

"Look, Lily, I can make the light go fast!" Tim said. He pressed the switch on and off very quickly. The light blinked and blinked.

"That's fun, Tim, but be careful. Mom said the switch can get hot if we do that too much," Lily said. She was thoughtful. She remembered what Mom told them.

Tim did not listen. He wanted to have more fun. He pressed the switch faster and faster. He did not see the smoke coming out of the switch. He did not hear the crackle.

Suddenly, there was a loud bang. The switch broke and the light went out. Tim and Lily screamed. They were scared and sad. They broke the switch and the light.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the broken switch and the dark room. She was angry and worried. She hugged Tim and Lily and asked them what happened.

"We were playing with the switch, Mom. We made the light go on and off. But then the switch got hot and it broke. We're sorry, Mom," Tim and Lily said. They felt bad. They knew they did something wrong.

Mom sighed. She was not happy, but she loved Tim and Lily. She said, "I'm glad you're okay, but you should not play with the switch. The switch is not a toy. It can be dangerous. You could have hurt yourself or started a fire. You should listen to me when I tell you something. Do you understand?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They understood. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We won't play with the switch again. We'll listen to you next time."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I forgive you. But you have to help me fix the switch and the light. And you have to drink some water. You must be thirsty after all that playing."

Tim and Lily agreed. They drank some water and helped Mom fix the switch and the light. They learned their lesson. They were more thoughtful and careful. They did not play with the switch anymore. They played with their other toys instead. They had fun and they were safe.

"Who is having the party?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Maybe we can ask someone," Lily said.

They walked around the park, looking for someone who knew about the party. They saw a boy with a red hat and a blue shirt. He was holding an invitation in his hand. He looked happy.

"Hi, can we talk to you?" Tom said.

"Sure, what do you want?" the boy said.

"We saw the sign for the party. Is it your party?" Lily said.

"No, it's not my party. It's Sam's party. He is my friend. He gave me this invitation," the boy said, showing them the paper.

"Can we have an invitation too?" Tom said.

"Sorry, no. Sam only gave invitations to his friends. You are not his friends. You are strangers. Go away," the boy said. He was rude and mean.

"Let's wait until he is not looking. Then we can take his invitation. He is careless. He will not notice," Tom said.

"OK, let's do that. But we have to be quick and quiet," Lily said.

They hid behind a tree and watched the boy. He was playing with a ball. He threw the ball high in the air and ran to catch it. He did not pay attention to his invitation. It was on the bench next to him.

Tom and Lily saw their chance. They sprang from behind the tree and ran to the bench. They grabbed the invitation and ran away. They were fast and sneaky.

"Yay, we did it! We are smart and clever! Let's go to the party!" Lily said.

Lily loved to read books. She had many books in her room. Some books had pictures, some books had stories, some books had words. Lily liked to learn new words. She had a big book with many words. It was a dictionary.

One night, Lily wanted to read her dictionary. She took it from her shelf and went to her bed. She turned on her lamp and opened the book. She saw many words and their meanings. She tried to read them, but some words were hard. She did not know how to say them or what they meant.

She asked her mom for help. Her mom came to her room and looked at the book. She smiled and said, "Lily, this is a very good book, but it is not for bedtime. This book is for when you want to study or write. It has many words that you will learn when you are older. But now, you need to sleep. Why don't you choose another book, a book with a story or a picture?"

Lily did not want to quit. She wanted to read her dictionary. She said, "No, mom, I want to read this book. I want to learn new words. Please, help me read this book." Her mom said, "Lily, I know you are curious and smart, but you also need to rest. Reading this book will not help you sleep. It will make your head hurt and your eyes tired. You can read this book tomorrow, when the sun is up. But now, it is dark and you need to sleep. Please, put this book away and choose another book."

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want to put her dictionary away. She wanted to read it. She said, "No, mom, I don't want to sleep. I don't want another book. I want this book. Please, let me read this book." Her mom said, "Lily, I am sorry, but you have to listen to me. This is not a good time to read this book. You are not being nice or respectful. You are being stubborn and rude. If you don't put this book away and go to sleep, I will take it away from you and you will not see it again."

Lily was scared and sorry. She did not want to lose her dictionary. She liked her dictionary. She also liked her mom. She did not want to make her mom angry or sad. She realized that she was wrong. She said, "Mom, I am sorry. I was not nice or respectful. I was stubborn and rude. I will put this book away and go to sleep. I will read it tomorrow, when the sun is up. Can you please forgive me and hug me?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily, I forgive you and I love you. You are a good girl and a good reader. I am proud of you for wanting to learn new words. But you also need to learn when to stop and when to listen. Reading is fun and important, but so is sleeping and obeying. You can read your dictionary tomorrow, but now, you need to sleep. Here, let me hug you and tuck you in. Good night, Lily."

Lily hugged her mom and said, "Good night, mom. I love you. Thank you for helping me and teaching me. I will sleep well and dream of new words." She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She was happy and peaceful.

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of moderation, obedience and respect. It shows that reading is good, but not at the expense of sleep and health. It also shows that listening to parents and following their rules is important and respectful. It also shows that apologizing and forgiving are signs of love and kindness.

Once upon a time, there were two furry animals - a squirrel and a mouse. The mouse was playing in a tiny stream near a tree, when the squirrel noticed her.

"Hey!", said the squirrel. "Let's have some fun together!"

The mouse, excited, looked up at the squirrel and asked what they should do.

The squirrel had an idea. He told the mouse: "Let's shoot acorns at each other!"

The mouse wasn't so sure. She thought it sounded like a silly game.

The squirrel, determined, said: "Come on! It will be fun!"

The mouse wasn't convinced and said "No, I don't think it's a good idea."

The squirrel, annoyed, said "It's only a bit of fun - it won't hurt anyone."

But the mouse was right. Shooting acorns could be dangerous and the squirrel soon realised this. So, instead, they spent the rest of the day exploring the stream, collecting stones and looking at pretty plants.

The moral of the story is this: it's always best to be careful and think twice before doing things that could be dangerous.

But then Susan felt a tug on her waist. She looked up and saw it was a tall, terrible tree. It was shaking and growing bigger. Susan was scared and said, "What are you doing?" 

The tree said, "I'm trying to get you to help me. My leaves are so dry and I don't have enough water." 

Susan nodded and smiled. She helped the tree get water from the nearby stream. Susan had saved the day and the tree seemed very happy.

One day in the forest, there was a bald lion. He was feeling very sad. He said to himself, "I don't want to be bald anymore!"

He lay down in the grass and waited for someone to come and save him. He wanted to have a nice, furry mane.

Soon, a little girl named Emma came walking through the forest. She spotted the bald lion and said, "Oh, what's wrong? Are you feeling sad, poor lion?"

The lion said, "Yes, I am feeling very sad. Can you help me? Can you help me save my bald head?"

Emma was very brave. She thought for a moment, then said, "Yes, I will help you! I will find something for you to use on your head."

She ran off and returned shortly after with a lovely, bright green scarf, just the right size for a lion's head. She wrapped the scarf around the lion's head, making him look like he had a full and fluffy mane.

The bald lion was so happy and thanked Emma for saving him. "From now on, I will always be a proud, beautiful and furry lion!" he said. And from that day forward, the lion always wore his green scarf with pride.
